newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian wine goes down a treat in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Italian wine goes down a treat in Japan.

text.p: Italian wine exports to Japan had a boom year in 1996 with sales up 60.2 percent on 1995 for a total value of 94.62 billion lire ($55.5 million), the Lombardy Foreign Trade Centre said on Wednesday.

Wine counts for only a fraction of total Japanese imports from Italy, at 1.1 percent. But the recent sales rise has put Italy into second place among wine exporters to the country, behind France but ahead of Germany, the Centre said in a statement.
There were many reasons for the appeal of Italian wine to the tastebuds of Japanese consumers, said Paolo Makiyama, chairman of the Milan office of the International Nikken trading company.
"Above all, the great number of tourists visiting Italy in recent years have learned to appreciate not just the country's artistic and monumental beauty but also its cuisine and wines.
"In fact, Japan's mass-media is really pushing Italian cuisine just like it happened for French cuisine some time ago," he said.
"For the Japanese, it is important that the wine is dry, not fizzy and especially white. But red wine also goes down well as long as it's strong," he added.
